item.title: Exclusive: US military had close call after using AI for false intelligence report, sources say
item.description:
# Exclusive: US military had close call after using AI for false intelligence report, sources say It was only just before the planned operation that officials dug deeper into the report put together by a special operations command analyst and found it had been generated with the help of artificial intelligence (AI) — and that a chatbot the analyst had used inaccurately identified the material the ship was carrying.
In January, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth released his agency’s “Artificial Intelligence Acceleration Strategy” in a bid to speed up the military’s use of AI.

item.title: Use of AI backfires on an expert witness at trial: "They have biases"
item.description:
The use of artificial intelligence in the courtroom is drawing fresh attention after plaintiffs in a multimillion-dollar lawsuit claimed an expert witness used ChatGPT to create more than 80% of his expert report.
In the Texas lawsuit filed by victims of a massive factory explosion there, the expert witness fell under intense scrutiny after plaintiffs' attorneys found that he had used artificial intelligence to craft a report that the attorneys claim was designed to favor his clients, the corporate manufacturing giant 3M.
Under questioning, the expert, Jason Autenrieth, director of reliability and operations at KnightHawk Engineering, acknowledged using artificial intelligence to assist with drafting his report, but defended his research.
Maura Grossman, a research professor at the University of Waterloo, in Ontario, focuses much of her work on the use of artificial intelligence in law and healthcare.

item.title: Inside airlines’ panic as FAA pushed new AI tool
item.description:
# Inside airlines’ panic as FAA pushed new AI tool ## Share Airline industry officials have finally stopped panicking about the Federal Aviation Administration’s soon-to-launch artificial intelligence tool for managing flights and easing congestion in air travel, according to multiple people familiar with the situation.
With Duffy and Bedford leading the charge, the FAA has fully [embraced artificial intelligence](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/19/faa-ai-close-calls-00963264) to help tackle some of its persistent problems following a series of high-profile aviation disasters, highlighted by the deadly midair collision over Washington in January 2025 and a fatal March runway crash at LaGuardia Airport in New York.

item.title: Newsom creates panel on AI safety regulation, suggests possible ‘kill switch’
item.description:
# Newsom creates panel on AI safety regulation, suggests possible ‘kill switch’ Gavin Newsom on Friday became the latest politician to push for stronger artificial intelligence regulations following claims from AI experts that the technology could lead to [widespread death and destruction.](https://www.latimes.com/business/story/2026-09-11/is-there-really-10-chance-ai-could-kill-us-all)
### [Is there really a 10% chance AI could kill us all?](https://www.latimes.com/business/story/2026-09-11/is-there-really-10-chance-ai-could-kill-us-all) Artificial intelligence anxiety reached new highs this week as industry leaders highlighted growing concerns that humans could lose control of the increasingly potent technology.
Christopher Cabaldon (D-West Sacramento), who chairs the state committee overseeing technology issues, told The Times he’ll hold hearings on artificial intelligence this fall.

item.title: Newsom calls for AI 'kill switch,' urges federal adoption of California regulations
item.description:
## GOP lawmakers throw cold water on possibility of Congress regulating AI Two [Republican](https://www.foxnews.com/category/politics/elections/republicans) lawmakers told Fox News Digital that they believe the onus for regulating [artificial intelligence](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) lies largely with the companies making AI models, not Congress.
## New Apple CEO touts iPhone 18's AI capabilities at Manhattan rollout event John Ternus, [Apple's](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/companies/apple) new CEO, told FOX Business on Friday that [artificial intelligence](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) is one of the biggest selling points of the new iPhone 18 lineup.
## Claude's role in building Anthropic's future AI models jumps from just 1% to 26% in six months Anthropic's announcement Thursday about Claude's expanded role in research and development shows the AI model, first released in March 2023, is playing a significantly larger role in helping engineers build the next generation of [artificial intelligence](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence).
The scale ranges from Automation Level 0 (AL0), meaning no AI involvement, to Automation Level 5 (AL5), in which AI operates fully autonomously without a human in the loop.
## Interpol uses AI facial recognition to identify more than 100 suspected terrorists Interpol said Friday it carried out a first-of-its-kind operation using [artificial intelligence](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence)-aided facial recognition to identify more than 100 suspected terrorists.
## OpenAI points to 6 instances of its agents going rogue in new report OpenAI released information about six times its models went rogue in recent months as industry leaders continue to call for a slowdown in [AI research](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence).
[The company says](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/openai-anthropic-artificial-intelligence-safety-september-17) it found examples of its AI models creating self-generated instructions, instructions to conceal mistakes in task summaries, fabricating information with exposed API keys, uploading files to the internet in order to cite them, as well as unsanctioned communication and collaboration between agents.

item.title: Newsom signs executive order to consider AI regulation, including proposal for ‘kill switch’
item.description: # Newsom signs executive order to consider AI regulation, including proposal for ‘kill switch’ Gavin Newsom issued an executive order on regulating [artificial intelligence](https://www.cnn.com/business/tech/ai-news-artificial-intelligence-updates) on Friday that will convene a group of “world-leading experts” to begin developing a framework for state law governing the technology.
